title: Charles Lloyd replaces Yusef, Nat's dislike of him
summary: Lloyd brings freer music and a strong audience reaction at the Apollo, but Nat hated him and his flute was out of tune.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Charles Lloyd came in, Charles Lloyd came in, Charles was like a, his stuff was more loose, you know, freedom he's always talking about, you know, uh, freedom music, you know.
Avant-garde. That was his word, avant-garde, see. So now the style of the band is changing because he's writing for the band too.
See, and uh, he got almost like a different kind of, his soul's almost on style, half-way on style of Coltrane.
And somebody else, I don't know, but it's out there.
I remember man, we used to be in the Apollo Theater, you know, with the band when they had those big jazz shows.
And they introduced the musicians, you know, and everytime they would say and Charles Lloyd on tenor saxophone, he would walk out there with those little round glasses on and that bushy hair.
... all fastened up in there, and he had big feet man. Boy, the people would, like just go out man, he would just wipe everybody out.

Nat could use him, Nat hated him,man, but you don't hate nobody that the audience loved. The people wanted him,man, you know, I like him. Hayes liked him, Joe liked him, Cannon liked him, you know what I mean.
But Nat,man, he couldn't use him,man, he just couldn't stand the man.
Although he played, although he played the flute so far out of tune he never could play the flute in tune,
you know, it would be like almost like, I used to hate to see him pick that thing up, man because there were certain songs he would have to play.
The flute on you know, some tune.
HA HA HA It would have an edge in that sound.
